translations.text: After Moses, the servant of the Lord, died, the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ attendant, and said:
“Moses my servant has died. Now rise and cross this Jordan, you and all your people, into the land that I will give to the Israelites.
Every place where your feet tread I will give to you, as I told Moses.
The wilderness and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates River, all the land of the Hittites, as far as the western sea toward the setting sun, will be your territory.
No one will stand against you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not abandon you or neglect you.
Be strong and courageous, for you will divide among this people the land that I swore to your ancestors to give them.

Now be strong and very courageous, keeping and doing everything according to the law, as Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may act wisely in everything you do.

This book of the law must not depart from your mouth. Meditate on it day and night, so that you may understand how to do everything written in it. Then you will prosper and make your ways straight, and then you will act wisely.
Look, I command you: be strong and courageous. Do not hesitate or be afraid, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”
Joshua commanded the scribes of the people, saying:

“Go through the camp of the people and give the people this command: ‘Prepare provisions for yourselves, for in three more days you will cross this Jordan to enter and possess the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, will give you as an inheritance.’”
Joshua spoke to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, saying:
“Remember the word of the Lord that Moses his servant commanded you, saying, ‘The Lord your God has settled you and given you this land.’

Your wives, your children, and your livestock will remain in the land that Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan. But you, all the mighty warriors, must cross over armed ahead of your brothers and fight alongside them,

until the Lord your God settles your brothers as he has settled you, and they too inherit the land that the Lord your God will give them. Then each of you may return to your own inheritance and possess it, the land that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave you on this side of the Jordan, to the east.”
They answered Joshua, saying, “We will do everything you command us, and we will go wherever you send us.
Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we will obey you. Only may the Lord our God be with you as he was with Moses.”
Any man who disobeys you and does not listen to your words, whatever command you give him, shall die. Only be strong and courageous.

Joshua son of Nun sent two young men from Shittim to spy out the land secretly, saying, “Go and spy out the land and Jericho.” The two young men went to Jericho, entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and lodged there.
The king of Jericho was informed: “Look, men from among the Israelites have come here tonight to spy out the land.”
The king of Jericho sent word to Rahab, saying, “Bring out here the men who came to you and entered your house tonight, for they have come to spy out the whole land.”
The woman took the two men and hid them. She spoke to them and said, “Men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
When the gate was being closed at the twilight of morning, the men went out. I do not know where they went. Pursue them quickly; perhaps you will catch them.”
She took them up onto the roof and hid them under bundles of flax that she had piled up on the roof.
The men pursued them along the road to the Jordan, to the ford. The gate was shut when the pursuers had gone out after them.
Before they had gone to sleep, she went up to them on the roof.
She said to them, “I know that the Lord has given you this land, because fear of you has fallen upon us, and all who live in this land have lost heart because of you.
For we heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you destroyed.
When we heard this, we were terrified in our hearts, and none of us had any breath left because of you, for the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on earth below.
Now swear to me by the Lord God that, since I am showing you kindness, you too will show kindness to my father’s household, and give me a trustworthy sign.
Keep my father’s household alive, along with my mother, my brothers, my sisters, and all that belongs to them, and save my life from death.”

The men said to her, “Our lives in place of yours, even to death, if you do not tell anyone about this matter concerning us.” And she said, “When the Lord hands this city over to you, show me kindness and faithfulness.”
She lowered them by a rope through the window, because her house was in the city wall, and she lived in the wall.
She said to them, “Go into the hill country so that the pursuers do not encounter you. Hide there for three days, until the pursuers return from following you, and then go on your way.”
The men said to her, “We are released from the oath you made us swear.

“Look, we will enter a part of your city. You shall put up a scarlet cord as a sign and tie it to the window through which you let us down. Gather your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father’s household to you in this house.”

Anyone who goes outside your house will be responsible for his own life, and we will be released from this oath of yours. But for everyone who is with you in your house, we will be responsible if anyone lays a hand on them.
But if anyone wrongs us and you reveal these words of ours, we will be released from this oath of yours.”
She said, “Let it be according to your words; so let it be.” She sent them away, and they went, and she tied a red sign in the window.
They went and came to the hill country and stayed there for three days, until the pursuers returned. The pursuers searched the whole road but did not find them.
The two young men returned, came down from the mountain, crossed over, and reached Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, “The Lord God has handed the whole land over to us, and all the inhabitants of the land are terrified of us.”
Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the Israelites. They camped there before crossing.
After three days, the scribes went through the camp.
They instructed the people, saying, “When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and our priests and the Levites carrying it, set out from your places and follow it.

But there must be a greater distance between you and them; we will leave a space of about two thousand cubits. Do not approach it, so that you may know the road you are to take, for you have not traveled this road before.”
Joshua said to the people, “Purify yourselves for tomorrow, because tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you.”
Joshua spoke to the priests and said, “Take up the ark of the covenant of the Lord and go ahead of the people.” The priests took up the ark of the covenant of the Lord and went ahead of the people.
And the Lord said to Joshua, “On this day I will begin to exalt you before all the children of Israel, so that they may know that just as I was with Moses, so I will also be with you.
Now command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, and say, ‘When you enter the edge of the waters of the Jordan, stand within the Jordan.’”
And Joshua said to the children of Israel, “Come here and hear the words of the Lord your God.”

And Joshua said, “By this you will know that the Lord is living among you and will utterly destroy before you the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites.
Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is crossing the Jordan ahead of you.
Now choose beforehand twelve men from among you, from the children of Israel, one man from each tribe.”
When the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth enter the water of the Jordan, the water flowing down from above shall cease and stand in a single heap.
And when the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, the priests carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord ahead of all the people.

And as the priests carrying the ark of the covenant entered the Jordan, the feet of the priests carrying the ark were dipped into the edge of the waters of the Jordan. The Jordan was overflowing both its banks, as it does during the days of the wheat harvest.

And the waters coming down from above stood in a single mass, cut off very, very far from the city of Adam, which is part of Kiriath-jearim. Those flowing downstream went down into the sea of the Arabians, the Salt Sea, until they had completely receded. And the people stood opposite Jericho.

And the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood firmly on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, and all the children of Israel crossed on dry ground until all the people had finished crossing the Jordan.
And when all the people had finished crossing the Jordan, the Lord spoke to Joshua and said,
Take for yourself twelve men from that people, one man from each tribe.

“Give them a command and say, ‘Take for yourselves twelve ready stones from there, from the middle of the Jordan, from the places where the priests’ feet stood. Carry them with you and place them in your camp, where you will camp tonight.’”
Joshua called twelve men from among the distinguished men of the Israelites, one from each tribe.

And Joshua said to them, “Go ahead of me into the middle of the Jordan, before the Lord, and let each man take a stone from there and lift it onto his shoulders, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
So that they may stand as a lasting sign for you, when your son asks you in days to come, “What do these stones mean to you?”

You shall tell your son and say, ‘Because the river Jordan receded before the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth. As it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan receded.’ And these stones shall be a memorial for you among the children of Israel forever.”

And the children of Israel did as the Lord commanded Joshua. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, as the Lord instructed Joshua when the children of Israel had finished crossing. They carried them with them to the camp and placed them there.
And Joshua set up another twelve stones there in the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord had stood. And they are there to this day.

And the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood there in the middle of the Jordan until Joshua had finished telling the people everything the Lord had commanded Joshua, in accordance with everything Moses had commanded Joshua. And the people hurried and crossed.
And when all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the twelve stones also crossed ahead of them.
The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh also crossed, armed, ahead of the children of Israel, as Moses had commanded them.
Forty thousand men armed for battle passed before the Lord to wage war against the city of Jericho.
On that day the Lord exalted Joshua before the whole nation of Israel, and they feared him as they had feared Moses, for as long as he lived.
And the Lord spoke to Joshua and said:
“Command the priests who are carrying the ark of the covenant of testimony to come up out of the Jordan.”
And Joshua commanded the priests, saying, “Come up out of the Jordan.”

And when the priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s covenant came up from the middle of the Jordan and set their feet on dry ground, the water of the Jordan returned to its place and flowed as it had before, throughout its whole channel.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and the Israelites camped at Gilgal, on the eastern side of Jericho.
And Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan.
And he said to the Israelites, “When your children ask in days to come, ‘What are these stones?’
you shall tell your children, ‘Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground,’

because the Lord our God dried up the waters of the Jordan before them until they had crossed, just as the Lord our God did to the Red Sea, which the Lord our God dried up before us until we had crossed.”
So that all the nations of the earth may know that the Lord’s power is mighty, and so that you may worship the Lord your God at all times.

And when all the kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan toward the seacoast, and the kings of the Phoenicians who were along the seacoast, heard that the Lord God had dried up the Jordan River before the Israelites as they crossed, their hearts melted and they were terrified, and there was no wisdom at all left in them because of the Israelites.
At that time the Lord said to Joshua, “Make yourself a knife of flint, and sit down and circumcise the Israelites a second time.”

And Joshua made himself flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at the place called the Hill of the Uncircumcised. And this is how Joshua circumcised the Israelites who were on the journey there: Joshua circumcised all those among the people who had come out of Egypt who had not been circumcised at all.

And these are the people whom Joshua circumcised: the male children of all the people who had come out of Egypt, because all the fighting men had died there in the wilderness, on the journey after they came out of the land of the Egyptians.
For all the people who came out had been circumcised, as had all the people who were born in the wilderness on the journey after they came out of the land of the Egyptians.

For Israel wandered for forty-two years in the wilderness of Abdara, and because of this many of the fighting men who had come out of the land of the Egyptians were uncircumcised. They disobeyed God’s commandments, and the Lord decreed that they would not see the land he had sworn to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And he raised up their children in their place, and Joshua circumcised them, because they were uncircumcised, having remained uncircumcised on the journey.
And when the whole nation had been circumcised, they stayed quietly there in the camp until they recovered.
And the Lord said to Joshua, “On this day I have removed the reproach of the Egyptians from you.” And he called that place Gilgal, its name to this day.
And the Israelites camped there, and the Israelites celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, in the plain east of Jericho.
And on the morning after the Passover they ate from the grain of the land: unleavened bread and roasted grain on that very day.
The manna ceased after they ate the grain of the land, and the Israelites no longer found manna. They gathered the produce of the land of the Phoenicians that year.
While Joshua was at Jericho, he raised his eyes and saw a man standing before him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua approached him and said, “Are you on our side or on the side of our enemies?”
He said to him, “I am the commander of the Lord’s army, and I have now come.”
Joshua fell on his face and bowed in worship, and said to him, “Lord, what command will you give your servant?”
The commander of the Lord’s army said to Joshua, “Remove your shoes from your feet, because the place where you are standing is holy.” And Joshua did so.
Jericho was closed and fortified against the Israelites. No one went out of it, and no one entered.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Look, I am giving Jericho into your hands, along with its king and its mighty warriors.”

“But you, lead all the warriors around it with the jubilee trumpet when you hear the sound of the horn trumpet. When you blow the trumpet, all you fighting men shall march around the city once. Do this for six days.”
“Seven priests shall carry seven jubilee horn trumpets before the ark. On the seventh day you shall march around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the horn trumpets.”
“All the people shall shout together, and when they shout, the walls of the city shall collapse by themselves beneath them. All the people shall enter the city, each advancing straight ahead.”
Joshua son of Nun went in to the priests and said to them, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven jubilee horn trumpets before the ark of the Lord.”
He spoke with them and said, “Command the people to go and march around the city, and let the warriors go armed before the ark of the Lord.”

When he had instructed the people, the seven priests who carried the seven sacred trumpets were likewise to pass before the Lord and sound them loudly, and the ark of the covenant of the Lord was to go behind them.
“The warriors shall go ahead, and the priests and those who blow the horn trumpets shall go as the rear guard behind the ark of the Lord, blowing the horn trumpets.”

Joshua gave the people a command, saying, “Do not shout, let no one hear your voice, and let no word come out of your mouth until the day when he himself gives the signal to shout. Then you shall shout.”
After the ark of the Lord’s covenant had gone around the city, it returned to the camp and spent the night there.
On the second day Joshua rose at dawn, and the priests took up the ark of the Lord.

The seven priests took seven sacred trumpets and went before the Lord. The priests blew the trumpets, and all the rest of the crowd did so as well. They returned again to the camp, and then the warriors entered, along with the rest of the crowd behind the ark of the Lord’s covenant. They went along blowing the horn trumpets.
On the second day they marched once around the city, close to it, and returned again to the camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they rose at daybreak and marched around the city seven times in the same way.
On the seventh time around, the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua said to the Israelites, “Now shout, because the Lord has delivered this city into our hands.”

“The city shall be under a curse from the Lord of hosts, both the city itself and everything in it. But spare Rahab the prostitute and everyone in her house, because she hid the messengers whom we sent.”
“But you must beware of the things under the curse, lest you desire them and take anything from them, bringing the camp of the Israelites under a curse and destroying us.”
“All gold, silver, bronze, and iron shall be holy to the Lord and shall go into the Lord’s treasury.”

The people shouted, and the priests blew the trumpets. When the people heard the sound of the trumpet, all the people together gave a great, mighty shout, and the wall fell down all around. All the people went up into the city, each straight ahead, and they captured the city.
They devoted it to destruction and put everything in the city to the sword, from men to women, from young to old, and from cattle to sheep and donkeys.
Joshua said to the two young men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house and bring her out of there, along with everything that belongs to her, as you swore to her.”

The two young men who had spied out the city went into the woman’s house and brought out Rahab the prostitute, her father, her mother, her brothers, everything that belonged to her, and her entire clan. They settled her outside the camp of Israel.
The city was burned with fire, along with everything in it, except the gold, silver, bronze, and iron, which they handed over to be brought into the Lord’s treasury.

Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and everything that belonged to her. She has lived among Israel to this day, because she hid the spies whom Joshua sent that day to spy out Jericho.

On that day Joshua pronounced a curse on Jericho and said, “Cursed before the Lord be the man who rises up and rebuilds the city of Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he shall lay its foundations, and at the cost of his youngest he shall erect the gates of its wall.” And Azan of Bethel did so: at the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundations, and at the cost of Zertsel his youngest he erected its gates.
The Lord was with Joshua, and his name was known throughout the whole land.

The children of Israel committed a transgression and stole some of the things devoted to destruction. Achar son of Carmi, son of Zimri, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of the things devoted to destruction, and the Lord became fiercely angry with the children of Israel.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is opposite Bethel, and said to them, “Spy out Ai.” The men went up and spied out Ai.
They returned to Joshua and said, “Do not let all the people go up. Let about two or three thousand men go up and besiege the city. Do not take all the people there, for they are few.”
About three thousand of the people went up there, and they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai killed thirty-six of them and pursued them from the gate until they crushed them, striking them down on the descent. The people’s hearts failed, and they became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown on the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, he and the elders of Israel. They put dust on their heads.

Joshua said, “I beg you, Lord, Lord, why did your servant ever bring this people across the Jordan, to hand them over to the Amorites and destroy us? It would have been better if we had settled and lived there beside the Jordan.
Alas, Lord! What shall I do now, since Israel has bowed its neck before its enemies?
When the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land hear of it, they will surround us and wipe us from the land. And what will you do for your great name?”
The Lord said to Joshua, “Stand up! Why are you lying fallen on your face?”
“The people have sinned and broken my covenant, which I made with them. They have stolen and taken some of the things devoted to destruction, lied, and put them among their own possessions.”

And the Israelites will no longer be able to stand against their enemies, but will turn their backs before their enemies, because they have come under the ban. I will no longer be with you unless you remove the things under the ban from among you.

Rise, consecrate the people, and have them consecrate themselves for tomorrow. Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Things under the ban are among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove the things under the ban from among you.

You shall all assemble in the morning according to your tribes. The tribe that the Lord identifies shall come forward by clans; the clan that the Lord identifies shall come forward by households; and the household that the Lord identifies shall come forward man by man.

And whoever is found with the things under the ban shall be burned with fire, together with his entire household and everything he has, because he has transgressed the Lord’s covenant and committed lawlessness among Israel.
Joshua rose early in the morning and brought the people forward according to their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was identified.
The tribe of Judah came forward by clans, and the clan of Zerah was identified. The clan of Zerah came forward man by man, and Zambri was identified.
His household came forward man by man, and Achar, son of Carmi, son of Zambri, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was identified.
Joshua said to Achar, “My son, give glory today to the Lord, the God of Israel, and make confession. Tell me what you have done, and do not hide it from me.”
Achar answered Joshua, “Truly, I have sinned before the Lord, the God of Israel. This is what I did:

I saw among the spoils a beautiful patterned cloak, two hundred two-drachma pieces of silver, and a bar of gold whose weight was fifty two-drachma pieces. I coveted them and took them. Look, they are hidden under the earth in my tent, and the silver is hidden beneath them.”
Joshua sent men as messengers, and they ran to the tent in the camp. There the things lay hidden in his tent, with the silver beneath them.
They took them out of the tent, brought them to Joshua and the elders of Israel, and laid them before the Lord.

Joshua took Achar, the son of Zerah, and brought him out to the valley of Achor, along with his sons, his daughters, his ox, his donkey, all his sheep, his tents, and all his possessions. All Israel went with him, and he brought them to the valley of Achor.
Joshua said, “Why have you brought ruin upon us? May the Lord bring ruin upon you this very day.” All Israel stoned him with stones, and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
They piled a great heap of stones over them, which remains to this day. The Lord turned away from his fierce anger. For this reason he called it the valley of Achor, as it is called to this day.

The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or alarmed. Take all the fighting men with you, rise, and go up to Ai. Look, I am giving into your hands the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.”
And you shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, but you shall take its spoils and its livestock as plunder. Set an ambush behind the city.
Joshua and all the fighting people rose to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out by night.
He commanded them, saying, “See that you lie in ambush behind the city. Do not be too far from the city, and all of you be ready.
“I and all the people with me will approach the city. When the inhabitants of Ai come out against us as they did before, we will flee before them.”
When they come out after us, we will draw them away from the city, and they will say, ‘They are fleeing before us as they did the first time.’ And when we flee before them,
you shall rise from the ambush, enter the city, and strike the city. The Lord, the God of Israel, will deliver them into our hands.”
And when we take the city, you shall burn it with fire. You shall act according to this instruction. Look, I have commanded you.
Joshua sent them away, and they went to the ambush and hid between Bethel and Dan, on the western side of Ai. Joshua spent that night among the people.
Joshua rose early in the morning and mustered the people. He and the elders of Israel went up against Ai ahead of the people.

All the fighting troops went up with them. They advanced and came opposite the city on its eastern side, while those lying in ambush were on the western side of the city. They camped north of Ai, with a valley between them and Ai.
He took five thousand men and placed them in ambush between Beth-aven and the sea of Ai.
He stationed the people and the entire army north of the city, with their rear guard on the western side of the city. Joshua spent that night in the middle of the valley.

When the king of Ai saw this, he hurried, rose early, and went out against them. The men of the city went to meet them in battle, he and all his people, at the appointed time, facing the Arabah. He did not know that an ambush had been laid for him behind the city.
When Joshua saw this, he turned back, and all Israel turned back before them, and they fled along the road to the wilderness.
All the people of the land hurried to pursue them and pressed on after the Israelites, and they went away from the city.
No one remained in Ai or Bethel who did not press on after Israel. They left the city open and rushed after Israel.

The Lord said to Joshua, “Stretch out your hand with the spear you are holding toward the city, for I have delivered it into your hands, and those lying in ambush will come out quickly from their position.” Joshua stretched out his spear and his hand toward the city.
Those lying in ambush rose quickly from their position and came out as soon as he stretched out his hand. They entered the city, captured it, and hurried to burn the city with fire.

The inhabitants of Ai looked behind them and saw that the smoke of the city was rising to heaven. They no longer had anywhere to escape, either this way or that. The people who had hidden in the wilderness rose up against their pursuers.
When Joshua and all the people saw that those lying in ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city was rising to heaven, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.

The others came out of the city to meet them, so the men of Ai were caught in the middle of the army, with some on one side and others on the other. They struck them down until none of them remained alive or escaped.
They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

When the Israelites had finished slaughtering all the people of Ai, those in the fields and those in the mountains on the slopes, where they had pursued them, and all had fallen by the sword until they were utterly destroyed, Joshua returned to Ai and struck it with the sword.
Those who fell that day, men and women, numbered twelve thousand—all the inhabitants of Ai.
Joshua did not draw back the hand he had stretched out with the spear until he had devoted all the inhabitants of Ai to destruction,
except for the livestock and the plunder of the city, which the Israelites took as spoils according to the Lord’s command, as the Lord had commanded Joshua.
Joshua burned the city with fire and made it a mound of earth, uninhabited forever, as it remains to this day.

He hanged the king of Ai on a forked tree, and he remained hanging on the tree until evening. At sunset Joshua gave orders, and they took him down from the tree and threw him into a pit by the city gate. They piled a heap of stones over him, which remains to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal.

as Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded the Israelites, as it is written in the law of Moses: an altar of whole stones that no iron tool had touched. There he offered a burnt offering to the Lord and a sacrifice of deliverance.
And Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the law, the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the Israelites.

And all Israel, their elders, their judges, and their scribes went on either side opposite the ark, and the Levitical priests carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord. Both foreigners and natives were there. Half of them were near Mount Gerizim and half near Mount Ebal, as Moses, the servant of the Lord, had commanded, to bless the people first.
Then he read all the words of these laws, the blessings and the curses, according to everything written in the law of Moses.
There was not a word of all that Moses commanded Joshua that Joshua did not read aloud to the whole assembly of Israel—men, women, children, and the foreigners who had settled in Israel.

When all the kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan heard—the ones in the mountains, the ones in the plains, the ones along the entire coast of the Great Sea, and those near Lebanon—and the Hittites, Amorites, Girgashites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites,
They all came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel.
And the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
They acted cunningly, coming with provisions and preparations. They took old sacks on their shoulders and old wineskins that were torn and patched,
and the [?] of their shoes, their sandals, were old and patched on their feet, and their clothes were old on their bodies, and the bread for their provisions was dried out and worm-eaten.
They came to Joshua at the camp of Israel in Gilgal and said to Joshua and all Israel, “We have come from a distant land. Now make a covenant with us.”
And the Israelites said to the Horite, “Look, perhaps you live among us. How can we make a covenant with you?”
They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” And Joshua said to them, “Where are you from, and where have you come from?”
They said to him, “Your servants have come from a very distant land because of the name of the Lord your God, for we have heard of his name and everything he did to Egypt,
and everything he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan—to Sihon, king of Heshbon, and to Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
Our elders and all the inhabitants of our land spoke to us and said, ‘Take provisions for the journey, go to meet them, and say to them, “We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us.”’
For this bread of ours was warm when we took it from our homes as provisions on the day we left our homes and came to you, but now it has dried out and become worm-eaten.
And these wineskins, which we filled with wine, were new, but they have torn. Our clothes and shoes have worn out because of the very long journey.”
And the leaders took their provisions, but did not consult the Lord.
Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them to keep them alive, and the leaders of the people swore an oath to them.
Three days after they made the covenant with them, they heard that they were neighbors and lived right there among them.
The Israelites set out and came to their towns on the third day. Their towns were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and the towns of Jearim.
The Israelites did not fight them, because all the leaders of the people had sworn an oath to them by the Lord, the God of Israel. And all the people grumbled against the leaders.
All the leaders said to all the people, “We swore an oath to them by the Lord, the God of Israel, and we cannot break our word to them.”
Now let us do this for them: let them live and keep them, so that wrath does not come upon us because of the oath we swore to them.
The leaders said to them, “Let them live and become wood gatherers and water carriers for this entire people.” And they became woodcutters and water carriers, just as the leaders had told them.
Joshua summoned them all together and spoke to them, saying, “Why did you deceive me and say, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you are local people living among us?
Now you are cursed, and you shall never be without servants who cut wood and carry water for me and my God.”

They answered Joshua, saying, “We were clearly informed of everything the Lord your God commanded Moses his servant: to give you this land and to destroy all its inhabitants before you. We were very afraid for our lives because of you, and we did this.
Now, here we are in your hands. Do to us whatever pleases you and whatever you wish to do.”
They did so to them, and on that day Joshua saved them from the hands of the Israelites, and they did not kill them.
On that day he appointed them to be woodcutters and water carriers for all the people and for the altar of God, down to this day, at the place the Lord would choose.

When Adoni-bezek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and destroyed it, doing to Ai and its king just as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had surrendered to Joshua and Israel and were living among them,
they were greatly terrified, for they knew that Gibeon was a large city, like one of the royal capitals. It was larger than Ai, and all its men were mighty warriors.
Adoni-bezek, king of Jerusalem, sent word to Elam, king of Hebron, to Piram, king of Jarmuth, to Japhia, king of Lachish, and to Debir, king of Eglon, saying,
“Come up to me and help me, and let us wage war against Gibeon, because they have surrendered to Joshua and the Israelites.”

The five kings of the Jebusites—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon—gathered and went up, together with all their people. They encamped around Gibeon and besieged it.

The inhabitants of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at Israel’s camp in Gilgal, saying, “Do not withdraw your hand from your servants. Come up to us quickly, save us, and help us, because all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us.”
Joshua went up from Gilgal with the entire fighting force and all the mighty warriors.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for I will deliver them into your hands, and not one of them will be able to stand against you.”
Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched all night from Gilgal.
The Lord threw them into terror before Israel and struck them with a great defeat at Gibeon. They pursued them along the road down from Beth-horon and slaughtered them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled before the Israelites down the slope of Beth-horon, the Lord hurled hailstones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword in battle.

Then Joshua spoke to the Lord on the day when the Lord God delivered the Amorites into the hands of the Israelites, at the time when he crushed them at Gibeon and they were defeated before Israel. Joshua said, “Let the sun stand still opposite Gibeon, and the moon opposite the valley of Aijalon.”

The sun and the moon stood still in their places until God had taken vengeance on their enemies. Is this not written in the Book of the Upright? The sun stood still in the middle of the sky and did not move toward sunset until a whole day was completed.
There was no day like that, either before or afterward, when God listened to the voice of a man, for the Lord fought alongside Israel.
Joshua and all Israel with him returned to the camp at Gilgal.
Those five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua was informed, and they said, “The five kings have been found hiding in the cave there at Makkedah.”
And Joshua said, “Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and station men over them to guard them.”
“But do not stop pursuing your enemies. Catch up with their rear ranks, and do not let them enter their cities, for the Lord God has delivered them into our hands.”
When Joshua and all the Israelites had finished slaughtering them in a very great slaughter, until they were completely destroyed, the survivors who escaped from among them entered fortified cities.
All the people returned unharmed to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah, and not one of the Israelites muttered with his tongue.
And Joshua said, “Open the cave and bring the five kings out of the cave to me.”
And they did so and brought the five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

And when they brought them to Joshua, Joshua summoned all Israel and the leading warriors who went with him, and said to them, “Come forward and put your feet on their necks.” And they came forward and put their feet on their necks.
And Joshua said to them, “Do not be afraid of them or be dismayed. Be courageous and strong, for this is what the Lord will do to all your enemies against whom you fight.”
And Joshua killed them and hung all five of them on trees, and they remained hanging on the trees until evening.
And at sunset Joshua gave orders, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had fled for refuge. They rolled large stones over the cave, which remain to this day.

And they captured Makkedah that day and struck it with the edge of the sword, along with its king. They utterly destroyed it and every living being in it, and no survivor or fugitive remained from it. And he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
And Joshua and all Israel with him went from Makkedah to Libnah, and they besieged Libnah.

And the Lord delivered it into the hands of Israel, and he captured it and its king. He struck it with the edge of the sword, along with every living being in it, and not a single survivor or fugitive remained in it. And he did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
And Joshua and all Israel with him went from Libnah to Lachish, and he encamped against it and besieged it.
And the Lord delivered Lachish into the hands of Israel, and he captured it on the second day. He struck it with the edge of the sword and utterly destroyed it, as he had done to Libnah.
Then Elam, king of Gezer, came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his army with the edge of the sword, until no survivor or fugitive remained among them.
And Joshua and all Israel with him set out from Lachish to Eglon, and he encamped against it and besieged it. And the Lord delivered it into the hands of Israel.
And he captured it that day and struck it with the edge of the sword. They killed every living being in it that day, as they had done to Lachish.
And Joshua and all Israel with him set out from Eglon to Hebron, and he encamped against it.

And they captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword, along with its king and every living being in it, and there was no survivor in it. They did to it as they had done to Eglon, and they utterly destroyed it, every living being, and everything in it.
And Joshua and all Israel turned toward Debir and encamped against it.

They captured it, its king, and all its troops, and struck it with the edge of the sword. They utterly destroyed it and every living being in it, and did not leave a single survivor. As they had done to Hebron, so they did to Debir and its king, and as they had done to Libnah and its king.

Joshua struck the whole land—the hill country, the Negev, the lowlands, and Ashdoth—and all its kings. He left no survivor there, and they destroyed every living creature there, just as the Lord, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua slaughtered them from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and throughout the whole land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all their kings and their land at once, because the Lord, the God of Israel, fought alongside Israel.
Joshua and all Israel with him returned to the camp at Gilgal.
When Jabin king of Hazor heard this, he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings of Great Sidon in the hill country, in Rabbah opposite Chinnereth, in the plain, in Naphoth-dor, and along the coast.
The Canaanites on the eastern side, in the coastal regions of the Amorites, and the Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites below Hermon in Mizpah.
They came out, with their kings accompanying them, and a great army, as numerous as the sand on the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.
All those kings assembled and came together, and they camped together beside the waters of Merom to wage war against Israel.

The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, for tomorrow at this time I will hand them all over, defeated, before the Israelites. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
Joshua and the entire fighting force with him came upon them suddenly at the waters of Merom and fell upon them on the mountainside.

The Lord handed them over to Israel. They struck them down and pursued them as far as Sidon the Great, as far as Misrephoth-maim, and as far as the plain of Mizpah to the east. He slaughtered them until none of them remained alive.
Joshua did to them as the Lord had commanded him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that time Joshua turned back, captured Hazor and its king, and killed him, because Hazor had formerly ruled over all those kingdoms.
They struck down every living creature in it with the edge of the sword and destroyed them all. No living creature remained in it, and they burned Hazor with fire.
Joshua captured all the cities of those kingdoms and their kings, struck them down with the edge of the sword, and destroyed them, just as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded them.
But Israel did not burn any of their cities built on mounds, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

The Israelites took all its spoil and livestock as plunder for themselves, but they destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword until they had wiped them out. They did not leave a single living person among them.
Just as the Lord had commanded his servant Moses, and as Moses had commanded Joshua, so Joshua did. He failed to carry out nothing of all that Moses had commanded him.
Joshua took all that land: the hill country, the whole land of the Negev, the whole land of Goshen, the lowlands, the western region, the mountain of Israel, and its valley beside the mountain,
from Mount Halak and the ascents of Seir as far as Baal-gad, and the plain of Lebanon at the foot of Hermon. He captured all their kings and slaughtered them.
Joshua waged war against all those kings for many days.
There was no city that the Lord did not hand over to the Israelites, except the Hivites who lived in Gibeon. He took all the others in battle.
For it was the Lord who hardened their hearts to meet Israel in battle, so that they would be destroyed and shown no mercy, but would be destroyed as the Lord had told Moses.

At that time Joshua came and destroyed the Anakim in the hill country of Hebron, Debir, and Anab, and throughout the mountain country of Israel and the mountain country of Judah, together with their cities. Joshua destroyed them.
None of the Anakim remained among the Israelites. They remained only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
Joshua took the whole land, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua gave it to Israel as an inheritance by lot according to their tribes. And the land rested from war.

These are the kings whom Moses and the Israelites killed, taking possession of their land beyond the Jordan on the western side, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah on the eastern side:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon and ruled from Aroer to the Arnon Valley, at the edge of the valley, and over half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok ravine, the boundary of the Ammonites.

And the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinnereth on the east, the Arabah as far as the sea, as far as the Salt Sea on the east, by the road to Beth-jeshimoth, and from Teman, which lies below the slopes of Pisgah.
And the territory of Og king of Bashan, who remained from among the giants and lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei,
ruling over Mount Hermon and Salecah and all Bashan as far as the borders of Geshur and Maacah, and half of Gilead as far as the borders of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of the Lord and the Israelites defeated them, and Moses the servant of the Lord gave that land as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the Amorites whom Joshua and the Israelites killed beyond the Jordan, along the seashore of Gilead in the plain of Lebanon, as far as Mount Halak on the ascent to Seir. Joshua gave that land to the tribes of Israel as an inheritance according to their allotted portions,
in the hill country, in the plain, in the Arabah, on the slopes, in the wilderness, and in the Negeb: the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.
The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is near Bethel, one;
The king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one.
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Abera, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron, one; the king of Meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor in Naphath-dor, one; the king of Gelim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one. All these kings numbered twenty-nine.
Joshua was old and advanced in years, and the Lord said to Joshua, “You are old and advanced in years, and much land remains to be taken into possession.
This is the land that remains: all the territory of the Philistines,

Geshur, and the Canaanite land, from the uninhabited land opposite Egypt as far as the borders of Ekron on the right. It is counted as belonging to the Canaanites, to the five kings of the Philistines: those of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron, and to the Hivites.
From Teman, all the land of the Canaanites, Gaza, and the Sidonians as far as Aphek, as far as the borders of the Amorites.
and all the land of Arabah belonging to the Philistines, and all Lebanon toward the sunrise, from Gilgal at the foot of Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath;

all who inhabit the mountain region from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians—I will destroy them before the Israelites. But you must allot their land as an inheritance to Israel, as I commanded you.

And now divide this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh. You shall give it to them from the Jordan to the Great Sea toward the west, and the Great Sea shall form its boundary.

And for the two tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh who were with Reuben and Gad, who received their inheritance which Moses gave beyond the Jordan to the east, Moses, the servant of the Lord, allotted it to them:
from Aroer, which is on the bank of the Arnon ravine, including the city in the middle of the valley and all of Mishor, from Medeba to Dibon;
all the cities of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the borders of the Ammonites;
and the territory of Gilead, the territories of Geshur and Maacah, all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was left from the remnant of the giants, and Moses struck him down and destroyed him.
But the Israelites did not destroy the Geshurites, the Maacathites, or the Canaanites, and the king of Geshur and Maacah lived among the Israelites to this day.

But no portion or inheritance was given to the tribe of Levi, because the Lord, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as the Lord told them. These are the portions that Moses allotted to the Israelites at Araboth-Moab, beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
And Moses gave a portion to the tribe of Reuben according to their clans.
Their territory extended from Aroer, which stands opposite the Arnon valley, and included the city in the Arnon valley and all of Mishor;
and from Medeba to Heshbon, including all their cities in Mishor, Dibon, Bamoth-baal, and the houses of Baal-meon;
and Jahaz, Kedemoth, and Mephaath;
and Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth, and Sior on Mount Anak;
and Beth-peor, Ashdoth-pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth;

and all the cities of Mishor and all the kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. Moses struck him down, along with the rulers of Midian—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—and the rulers of the Parasionites [?] who lived in the land.
And the Israelites killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword in a single moment.
The boundary of Reuben's territory was the Jordan. This is the inheritance of the Reubenites according to their clans, their cities and villages.
And Moses gave a portion to the Gadites according to their clans.
Their territory included Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites, as far as Aroer, which is opposite Rabbah;
and from Heshbon to Ramoth by Mizpah and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;

and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon. The Jordan is the boundary as far as the shore of the Sea of Chinnereth, beyond the Jordan to the east.
This is the inheritance of the descendants of Gad according to their clans, with their cities and their surrounding lands.
And Moses gave a portion to the half-tribe of Manasseh, and it belonged to the half-tribe of the descendants of Manasseh according to their clans.
Their territory extended from Mahanaim and included all Bashan, the entire kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair in Bashan, sixty cities.

And half of Gilead, together with Ashtaroth and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were given to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, to half the descendants of Manasseh according to their clans.
These are the inheritances Moses allotted beyond the Jordan, in Araboth of Moab, on the eastern side of the Jordan opposite Jericho.
But Moses gave no inheritance to the tribe of Levi, because the Lord, the God of Israel, is himself their inheritance, as he told them.

These are the inheritances allotted to the Israelites in the land of the Canaanites, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of the Israelites allotted to them.
They allotted the inheritance by lot to the nine tribes and the half-tribe, as the Lord commanded through Joshua.
For Moses had given an inheritance to the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan, but he gave the Levites no inheritance among them.
For the descendants of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. No share of the land was given to the Levites, but only cities to live in and lands set apart for their livestock.
The Israelites did as the Lord commanded Moses, and they divided the land.

The descendants of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, “You yourself know what the Lord said to Moses the man of God concerning me and you at Kadesh-barnea.”
For I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of the Lord, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and we brought him a report in keeping with his wishes.
But my brothers who went up with me led the people's minds astray, while I continued to follow the Lord my God.
Moses swore on that day, saying, “The land you reached shall be an inheritance for you and your children forever, because you continued to follow the Lord my God.”

And now the Lord has sustained me, as he said. This is the forty-fifth year since the Lord spoke these words to Moses, while Israel wandered in the wilderness. And now, here I am today, eighty-five years old.
I am as strong today as when Moses sent me. Even now I am able to go into battle and come out.

And now I ask you for that mountain, as the Lord said on that day, for you yourself heard these words on that day. Now the Anakim are there, with fortified and very large cities. If the Lord is with me, I will destroy them, as the Lord told me.
Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as an inheritance.
Therefore Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, because he followed the command of the Lord, the God of Israel.
Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba. It was the chief city of the Anakim. And the land rested from war.
The boundaries of the tribe of the descendants of Judah, according to their families, extended from the borders of the Edomites, from the wilderness of Zin as far as Kadesh, toward the south.
Their southern boundary extended to the edge of the Salt Sea, from the ridge that slopes down toward the south.
And the boundaries pass to the ascent of Akrabbim, go around Zin, ascend from the south to Kadesh-barnea, go out to Hezron, extend past Addar, and turn around to the west of Kadesh.
They proceed to Azmon and extend as far as the ravine of Egypt, and the boundary ends at the sea. These are their southern boundaries.
The eastern boundary was the whole Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan. Their northern boundary began at the ridge of the sea and at the mouth of the Jordan.
The boundary reached Beth-hoglah, turned north toward Beth-arabah, and went up to the stone of Bohan, of the descendants of Reuben.

The boundary went up along the fourth part from the Valley of Achor toward the south, and went down to Gilgal, which is opposite the approach to [?], toward the south. The boundary reached the waters of En-shemesh, and its endpoint was the spring of En-rogel.

The boundary went up into the Valley of the Sons of Hinnom, along the southern side of Jebus—that is, Jerusalem. The boundary reached the summit of the mountain facing the Valley of Hinnom on the western side, at the northern edge of the land of the Rephaim.
The boundary goes up from the summit of the mountain to the spring of Naphtoah, crosses Mount Ephraim at Gai, and goes up to Baalah, that is, the city of Kiriath-jearim.

The boundary turns from Baalah westward toward Asares, to Mount Seir, passes around the northern side of the city of Kiriath-jearim, that is, Chesalon, descends to the City of the Sun, and passes southward.
The boundary crosses the northern side of Ekron. The boundaries go out to Shikkeron, pass beside the mountain of the land of Baalah, and cross as far as Jabneel. Their boundaries end toward the sea.
The Great Sea marks their boundary on the west. These are the boundaries of the descendants of Judah on every side, according to their clans.
To Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a portion among the descendants of Judah at God's command. Joshua gave him the city of Arba, the chief city of Anak, that is, Hebron.
Caleb son of Jephunneh destroyed them there—the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, Talmai, and Ahiman, the descendants of Anak.
From there Caleb went up against the inhabitants of Debir. Debir had formerly been called the City of Letters.
Caleb said, “Whoever captures the City of Letters and takes possession of it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as his wife.”
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
As she went, she consulted with him and said, “I will ask my father for a field.” She cried out from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, “What is the matter with you?”
She said to him, “Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negeb, give me Gulloth-maim.” Caleb gave her the upper Gulloth and the lower Gulloth.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Judah according to their clans.
Their cities were—the first city of the tribe of the descendants of Judah on the borders of Edom in the wilderness—Kabzeel, Edrei, and Jagur;
Kinah, Dimonah, and Adadah;
Kadesh and Ithnan-ziph;
Telem and Bealoth;
and the city of Asebon, that is, Hazor;
Amam, Shema, and Moladah;
Hazar-gaddah and Beth-pelet;
Hazar-shual and Beersheba, with their villages and their fields;
Baalah, Avvim, and Ezem;
Eltolad, Chul, and Hormah;
Ziklag, Madmannah, and Sansannah;
Lamoth, Shilhim, and Rimmon: twenty-nine cities with their villages.
In the lowlands: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, and Ramon.
and Zanoah and Adithaim and Enam
and Jarmuth and Adullam and Narmah and Socoh and Azekah
and Shaaraim and Gederah and their farms: fourteen cities and their villages.
Zenan and Hadashah and Migdal-gad
and Dilean and Mizpah and Joktheel
and Lachish and Bozkath and Eglon
and Cabbon and Lahmas and Caslom
And Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah: sixteen cities and their villages.
Libnah and Ether
and Iphtah and Ashnah and Nezib
and Keilah and Achzib and Mareshah and Elemum: nine cities and their villages.
Ekron and its villages and its farms
and from Ekron to Jemna, all the outskirts of Ashdod and their villages and their farms.
Gaza and its villages and its farms, as far as the torrent valley of Egypt; and the Great Sea marks the boundary.
And in the hill country: Shamir and Jattir and Socoh
and Dannah and Mount Hermon and the City of Letters, which is Debir
and Anab and Eshtemoa and Anim
and Goshen and Holon and Giloh: eleven cities and their villages.
Ereb and Eshan and Erumah
and Janum and Beth-tappuah and Aphekah
and Humtah and the city of Arba, which is Hebron, and Zior: nine cities and their villages.
Maon and Carmel and Ziph and Juttah
and Jezreel and Jokdeam and Zanoakim
and Gibeah and Timnah: nine cities and their villages.
Halhul and Beth-zur and Gedor

and Maarath and Beth-anoth and Eltekon: six cities and their villages. Tekoa and Ephrathah, which is Bethlehem, and Peor and Etam and Kulon and Tatami and Sores and Karem and Gallim and Bether and Manoko: eleven cities and their villages.
Kiriath-baal, which is Kiriath-jearim, and Rabbah: two cities, with their villages and their fields.
Beth-bardis, Beth-arabah, Madon, and Secacah,
and Nibshan, the cities of salt, and En-gedi: seven cities, with their villages.
The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the descendants of Judah could not fight against them. The Jebusites lived with the descendants of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.

The boundaries of the descendants of Joseph extended from the Jordan opposite Jericho, from the water opposite Jericho on the east, through the wilderness. They went up from Jericho into the mountainous region of the wilderness at Bethel-Luz,
and went out from Bethel-Luz and passed along the boundaries of Archi-Ataroth.
They went out westward into the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the boundaries of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Gezer, and their endpoint was toward the sea.
The descendants of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, received their inheritance.

The boundaries of the descendants of Ephraim were established according to their clans. The boundaries of their inheritance on the east extended from Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon and Gezer.
The boundaries passed westward to Michmethath on the north. The boundary turned eastward to Taanath-shiloh and passed eastward by Janoah.
And the boundary shall descend from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, and their villages shall pass by Jericho and extend to the Jordan.

From Tappuah the boundary shall pass westward to the ravine of Kanah, and its endpoint shall be at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim according to their clans.
There were also cities set apart for the descendants of Ephraim within the inheritance of the descendants of Manasseh—all these cities with their villages.

Ephraim did not destroy the Canaanites living in Gezer, and the Canaanites lived among Ephraim to this day, until Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, came up, captured the city, and burned it with fire. He wiped out the Canaanites and the Perizzites living in Gezer, and Pharaoh gave it to his daughter as a dowry. They became servants who paid tribute.

The boundaries of the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh were established, for he was Joseph’s firstborn. Machir, Manasseh’s firstborn and the father of Gilead, received the region of Gilead and Bashan, because he was a warrior.

The other descendants of Manasseh received their portions according to their clans: the descendants of Abiezer, the descendants of Helek, the descendants of Asriel, the descendants of Shechem, the descendants of Shemida, and the descendants of Hepher. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, according to their clans.
Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters. These are the names of Zelophehad’s daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They stood before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua son of Nun, and before the leaders, and said, “God commanded through Moses that an inheritance be given to us among our brothers.” And he gave them an inheritance, by the Lord’s command, among their father’s brothers.
Manasseh’s allotted portion fell in the plain of Ghabek [?], and Gilead and Bashan, which are beyond the Jordan.
For the daughters of the descendants of Manasseh inherited an allotted portion among their brothers, and the land of Gilead belonged to the remaining descendants of Manasseh.
The boundaries of the descendants of Manasseh extended from Asher-Michmethath, which is opposite Shechem. The boundaries went to Jamin and Asheb, at the spring of Tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah, on Manasseh’s boundary, belonged to the descendants of Ephraim.

The boundaries descended to the valley of Kanah, southward, opposite the valley of Jair, and the terebinth of Ephraim was in the midst of the city of Manasseh. Manasseh’s boundaries were north of the streambed, and their endpoint was the sea.
The southern side belonged to Ephraim and the northern side to Manasseh, and the sea was their boundary. They adjoined Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh had Beth-shan and its villages, Ibleam and its villages, the inhabitants of Endor and its villages, the inhabitants of Taanach and its villages, the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages, and the third part of Naphath and its villages.
The descendants of Manasseh could not destroy those cities, and the Canaanites began to live in that land.
When the descendants of Israel gained the upper hand, they made the Canaanites subject to them, but they did not destroy them completely.
The sons of Joseph turned to Joshua and said, “Why have you given me only one inheritance and one allotment, when I am a numerous people and God has blessed me?”
Joshua said to them, “If you are a numerous people, go up into the forest and clear for yourself the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, if the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you.”

The descendants of Joseph said, “The hill country of Ephraim is not enough for us, and there are the very best horses and weapons belonging to every Canaanite who lives in my land alongside me, in Beth-shean and its villages and in the Valley of Jezreel.”
Joshua spoke to the sons of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, and said, “You are a numerous people and have great strength. You shall not have only one allotment.

The forest shall be yours, for it is wooded, and you shall clear it. Its outer reaches shall be yours when you destroy the Canaanites, for even though they have fine horses and are stronger than you, you shall overcome them.”
The whole congregation of the sons of Israel gathered at Shiloh, and they set up the tent of testimony there. The land was subdued by them.
Seven tribes of the sons of Israel remained without having received their inheritance.
Joshua said to them, “How long will you be slack about going in to take possession of the land that the Lord, the God of our fathers, has given you?
Give me three men from each tribe, and I will send them out. They shall set out, pass through the land, and write a description of it for me, showing how it should be divided.”
They came to him, and he divided it into seven portions for them. Judah shall remain within their territory in the south, and the sons of Joseph shall remain within their territory in the north.
And you shall divide the land into seven parts and bring them here to me, and I will cast lots for you here before the Lord our God.

For the sons of Levi have no portion among you, because the priesthood of the Lord is their portion. Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh received their inheritance beyond the Jordan to the east, which Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave them.

The men set out and went, and Joshua instructed the men who were going to survey the land, saying, “Go through the land and survey it, then come back to me here, and I will draw lots for you before the Lord at Shiloh.”

The men went and traveled through the land. They surveyed the land and inspected it, and wrote a description of it in a book, in seven portions according to its cities. They brought it to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before the Lord, and there he divided the land among the sons of Israel according to their divisions.
The lot for Benjamin came out first, according to their clans. The boundaries of their allotment lay between Judah and the sons of Joseph.
Their boundary on the north began at the Jordan. The boundary shall rise from the south of Jericho toward the north, rise into the hill country westward, and end at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
From there the boundary shall pass to Luz, along the southern side of Luz, which is Bethel. The boundary shall descend to Ataroth-addar, on the mountainside south of Lower Beth-horon.

The boundary shall pass on and turn south along the side facing the sea, from the mountain opposite Beth-horon on the south. It shall end at Kiriath-baal, which is Kiriath-jearim, a city of the sons of Judah. This is the western side.
And the southern border begins at the edge of Kiriath-jearim, and the boundaries pass to Gai and extend to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

The boundary shall descend to the edge of the mountain opposite the valleys of the sons of Hinnom, which is the portion of Anak of the Rephaim to the north. It shall descend into the Valley of Hinnom, along the southern side of Jebus, and descend to the spring of En-rogel.
And they cross northward and pass to the spring at Shemesh, and turn toward Geliloth, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, and descend to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
And they pass behind Beth-arabah on the north and descend to the Arabah.

The boundary shall descend along the side of Beth-hoglah, north of the sea. The boundary shall end at the northern shore of the Salt Sea and at the southern end of the Jordan. These are their boundaries on the south.
And the Jordan forms the boundary on the eastern side. This is the inheritance of the descendants of Benjamin, with their boundaries all around, according to their clans.
The cities of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, according to their clans, were Jericho, Beth-hoglah, and Emek-keziz,
Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, and Ophrah,
Karem, Chephar-ammoni, and Geba:
twelve cities and their villages.
Gibeon, Ramah, and Beeroth,
and Mizpah, Chephirah, and Mozah,
and Rekem, Irpeel, and Taralah,
and Zela, Eleph, Jebus—that is, Jerusalem—Gibeath, and the city of Arem: fourteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the descendants of Benjamin according to their clans.
And the second lot fell to Simeon, to the tribe of the descendants of Simeon according to their clans, and their inheritance was within the allotment of the descendants of Judah.
Their allotted portion included Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah,
and Hazar-shual, Balah, and Ezem,
and Eltolad, Bethul, and Hormah,
and Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susim,
and Beth-labaoth and their farms: thirteen cities with their villages.
Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan: four cities with their villages.

And all the farms around those cities, as far as Baalath Beerammoth at the entrance to Ramath toward the south. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon according to their clans.

The inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon lay within Judah’s allotted portion, because the portion of the descendants of Judah was larger than theirs. So the descendants of Simeon received their inheritance within their allotted portion.
The third lot came out for Zebulun according to their clans, and the boundaries of their inheritance extended as far as Sarid.
Their boundaries were the sea and Maralah; they would reach Dabbesheth and meet the valley opposite Jokneam.
And they turn from Sarid eastward toward Beth-shemesh, to the boundary of Chisloth-tabor, and pass to Daberath and go up to Japhia.
From there they would turn toward the east, extending to the city of Katasim, and pass through Rimmon to Amatharim Annuah.
The boundaries would turn northward to Jekathon, and their endpoint would be in the valley of Iphtah-el,
and through Kattamath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun according to their clans: their cities and their villages.
The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the descendants of Issachar according to their family groups.
Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, and Shunem,
and Hapharaim, Shion, Ramath, Endanim, Renath, and Anareth,
And Rabbith and Kishion and Aemes.
and Ramath, En-gaddis, En-gaddah, and Beth-masem.
The boundaries would meet Tabor and Kasim on the seaward side, and Beth-shemesh, and their endpoint would be the Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Issachar according to their clans: their cities and their farms.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the descendants of Asher according to their clans.
And their boundaries were Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph,
and Amad and Mishal, and extended to Carmel toward the sea, and to Shihor and Balanah.

And they turned eastward to Beth-dagon and extended to Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el on the north. The boundaries entered Saphatha and Beth-emek, ran along the borders of Neiel, and passed to Cabul on the left side,
and to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Sidon the Great.
And the boundaries turned to Ramah, as far as the fortified city of the Tyrians. The boundaries turned to Susa, and their endpoint was the sea and the allotment of Achzib,
and Ammah, Aphek, and Rehob: twenty-two cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Asher according to their clans: their cities and their villages.
And the sixth lot fell to Naphtali, to the descendants of Naphtali according to their clans.
And their boundaries were Meleph, Maelon, Bersanaim, Armeh, Negeb, and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum, and their endpoint was the Jordan.
And the boundaries turned toward the sea to Aznoth-tabor and passed from there to Hukkok. They adjoined Zebulun on the south and Asher toward the sea, and Judah and the Jordan on the east.
And the fortified cities of the Tyrians were Tyre, Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth,
and Adami, Ramah, and Hazor,
and Kedesh, Edrei, and En-hazor,
and Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh: nineteen cities with their outlying settlements.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali according to their clans: the cities and their villages.
And the seventh lot fell to the tribe of the descendants of Dan according to their clans.
And the boundaries of their inheritance were Zorah and Eshtaol,
and Shaalabbin, Ithlah, and Timnah,
and Eltekeh, Baalath, and Bene-berak,
and the cities of Shemesh, Aijalon, Elon, and Ekron,
and Gibbethon, Jehud, and Gath-rimmon,
and from the Sea of Hawks and Bacrona, a boundary near Joppa.

And the territory of the descendants of Dan went beyond these. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Dan according to their clans: the cities and their villages. And the descendants of Dan did not destroy the Amorites who oppressed them in the hill country, and the Amorites did not allow them to descend into the valleys. The boundaries of their allotted territory were restricted by them. And the descendants of Dan went and fought against Leshem, captured it, struck it with the edge of the sword, took possession of it, and settled in it. They named Leshem Dan, after the name of their father.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Dan according to their families: these cities and their outlying settlements.

And they finished taking possession of the land according to their boundaries. And the Amorites continued to live in Aijalon and Shaalbim, but the hand of Ephraim grew heavy upon them, and they became their tributaries. And they went to inspect the land according to their boundaries. And the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
At the Lord’s command they gave him the city he had asked for, Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim. He built the city and lived in it.

These are the portions that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel divided by lot at Shiloh before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of testimony. And they went to inspect the land.
The Lord spoke to Joshua and said, “Speak to the Israelites and say:
‘Set aside the cities of refuge about which I spoke to you through Moses,

as a refuge for a killer who kills someone unintentionally and unknowingly. They shall be cities of refuge for you, so that the killer does not die at the hands of the avenger of blood before standing before the assembly for judgment.

He shall flee to one of those cities, stand at the entrance to the city gate, and explain his case to the elders of that city. The people shall take him in among them and give him a place, and he shall live with them.
If the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not hand the killer over to him, because he struck his neighbor unknowingly and had not hated him before.’

And he shall live in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment, until the high priest who serves in those days dies. Then the killer shall return and come to his own place and his own house, to the city from which he fled.
They set apart Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim; and the city of Arba, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

Beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they designated Bezer in the wilderness on the plain, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

These are the distinguished cities for all the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them, so that anyone who kills someone unintentionally may flee there and not die at the hands of the avenger of blood before standing before the assembly for judgment.
The heads of the families of the descendants of Levi approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families of the tribes of Israel.
They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan and said, “The Lord commanded through Moses that we be given cities to live in and their pasturelands for our livestock.”
At the Lord’s command, the Israelites gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands as an inheritance.

The lot fell to the clan of Kohath, and the descendants of Aaron, the priests among the Levites, received by lot thirteen cities from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon, and the tribe of Benjamin.
The remaining descendants of Kohath received by lot ten cities from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, the tribe of Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The descendants of Gershon received by lot thirteen cities from the clans of the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The descendants of Merari, according to their clans, received by lot twelve cities from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun.
The Israelites gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands by lot, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon, and the tribe of Benjamin gave these cities, which were designated by name and clan,
to the descendants of Aaron, from the clan of Kohath among the descendants of Levi, because the first lot fell to them.
They gave them Kiriath-arba, the chief city of Anak, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, and the pasturelands around it,
and its fields and its villages, which Joshua gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh as a possession,
And to the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron, a city of refuge for a killer, with its pasturelands, and Libnah with its pasturelands.
and Jattir with the lands set apart for it, and Eshtemoa with the lands set apart for it,
