and Holon with the lands set apart for it, and Debir with the lands set apart for it,
and Ain with the lands set apart for it, and Juttah with the lands set apart for it, and Beth-shemesh with the lands set apart for it: nine cities from those two tribes.
From the tribe of Benjamin, Gibeon with the lands set apart for it, and Geba with the lands set apart for it.
and Anathoth with its pasturelands, and Almon with its pasturelands: four cities.
All the cities of the descendants of Aaron, the priests, were thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
For the families of the descendants of Kohath, the Levites who remained among the descendants of Kohath, the cities of their allotment were from the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave them Shechem, a city of refuge for a manslayer, with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer with its pasturelands,
and Kibzaim with its pasturelands, and Upper Beth-horon with its pasturelands: four cities.
From the tribe of Dan, Eltekeh with its pasturelands, and Gibbethon with its pasturelands,
and Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands: four cities.
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach with its pasturelands, and Beth-shan with its pasturelands: two cities.
In all, ten cities with their pasturelands for the family of the remaining descendants of Kohath.

And to the descendants of Gershon, from the clans of the Levites, they gave from the half-tribe of Manasseh cities set apart for killers: Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands, and Beeshterah with its pasturelands—two cities.
And from the tribe of Issachar, Kishion with its pasturelands, and Daberath with its pasturelands,
and Jarmuth with its pasturelands, and the Spring of Letters with its pasturelands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Asher, Mishal with its pasturelands, and Abdon with its pasturelands.
and Helkath with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Naphtali, cities set apart for a manslayer: Kedesh in Galilee with its pasturelands, Hammoth-dor with its pasturelands, and Noemmon with its pasturelands: three cities.
All the cities of Gershon according to their families were thirteen cities with their pasturelands.

And for the family of the descendants of Merari, the other Levites, from the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun: Jokneam with its pasturelands, Kedesh with its pasturelands, Karta with its pasturelands,
Dimnah with its pasturelands, and Nahalal with its pasturelands: five cities.
And beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho, from the tribe of Reuben, cities of refuge for a manslayer: Bezer in the wilderness of Misor with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands,
Kedson with its pasturelands, and Mizpah with its pasturelands: four cities.
And from the tribe of Gad, cities of refuge for a manslayer: Ramoth in Gilead with its pasturelands, and Mahanaim with its pasturelands,
Heshbon with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands: four cities in all.
All the cities of the descendants of Merari according to their families, who remained from the tribe of Levi—their allotment was twelve cities.
All the cities of the Levites within the holdings of the Israelites were forty-eight cities, with their pasturelands surrounding those cities.

Cities with pasturelands surrounding the cities: it was the same for all those cities. And Joshua finished dividing the land according to its boundaries. The Israelites gave Joshua a portion according to the Lord’s command. They gave him the city he requested, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. Joshua built the city and lived in it. And Joshua took the flint knives with which he had circumcised the Israelites who had come out on the journey through the wilderness, for they had not been circumcised there in the wilderness, and he placed them in Timnath-serah.
And the Lord gave Israel all the land that he had sworn to give their fathers. They took possession of it and lived in it.
And the Lord gave them rest on every side, as he had sworn to their fathers. None of their enemies rose against them, for the Lord delivered all their enemies into their hands.
Not one of all the good things that the Lord had spoken to the Israelites failed; everything came to pass.
Then Joshua summoned the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
He said to them, “You yourselves have obeyed everything that Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded you, and you have listened to my voice in everything that I commanded you.
And you have not abandoned your brothers for all those days and even longer, up to this present day, and you have kept the commandments of the Lord your God.

And now the Lord our God has given your brothers rest, just as he told them. So now return to your homes, to the land of your possession, which Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave you beyond the Jordan.

But be very careful to carry out the commandments and the law that Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded you: to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul.”
Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their homes.

And to half the tribe of Manasseh Moses gave land in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave land among their brothers along the seacoast. And when Joshua sent them away to their homes, he blessed them.

He spoke to them and said, “They will go to their homes with great wealth, very much livestock, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and very much clothing.” They divided the spoils from their enemies with their brothers.

The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned and departed from the Israelites at Shiloh, in the land of the Canaanites, to go to the land of Gilead, the land of their possession, which they had inherited by the Lord’s command through Moses.

They came to Geliloth by the Jordan, which is in the land of Canaan, and the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar beside the Jordan, an altar impressive to look at.

The Israelites heard and said, “Look, the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar within the borders of the land of the Canaanites, at Geliloth by the Jordan, on the side opposite the Israelites.”
The Israelites heard this, and the Israelites assembled at Shiloh to go out and wage war against them.
The Israelites sent Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead.

With him were ten men from among the leaders, one leader from the heads of the ancestral families of each of the tribes of Israel. They were leaders of ancestral households, commanders of thousands in Israel.
They came to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, and spoke to them, saying,

“This is what the whole congregation of the Lord says: What are these offenses that you have committed against the Lord, the God of Israel, turning away from the Lord, building yourselves an altar, and rebelling against the Lord our God?
Is the sin of Peor a small thing to us? We have not been cleansed of it to this day, and plagues came upon the congregation of the Lord.
Yet you have turned away from the Lord today. If you rebel against the Lord today, tomorrow wrath will come upon all Israel.

Now, if the land of your possession is too small for you, cross over into the land of the Lord’s possession, where the Lord’s tabernacle is set up, and take a possession among us. Do not rebel against the Lord, and do not rebel against us by building yourselves an altar other than the altar of the Lord our God.
Did not Achan, the son of Zerah, commit an offense concerning the things under the ban, and wrath came upon the whole congregation of Israel? He was only one; did he alone die for his sins?”
The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered and spoke to the commanders of thousands, saying:
“The Lord is God, God; and God, God himself knows, and Israel itself shall know. If we have committed any offense against the Lord out of rebellion, may he not keep us alive this day.
And if we built ourselves an altar to rebel against our Lord, to offer burnt offerings on it or to make peace offerings on it, may the Lord himself call us to account.
Rather, we did this out of fear, saying, ‘Perhaps your children will speak to our children and say, “What have you to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?”’

‘The Lord has set the Jordan as a boundary between us and you, descendants of Reuben and descendants of Gad, and you have no share in the Lord.’ Thus your children will alienate our children so that they will not worship the Lord.
And we said, ‘Let us do this: build this altar, not for burnt offerings and not for sacrifices.’

Rather, this is to be a witness between us and you and our children after us, that we may perform the service of the Lord before him with our offerings, our sacrifices, and our peace offerings, and that your children may not say to our children in the future, ‘You have no share in the Lord.’

And we said, ‘If this ever happens and they speak to us or to our descendants in the future, they will say, “Look at the likeness of the Lord’s altar that our fathers made—not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you and among our children.”’

Far be it from us to rebel against the Lord today by building ourselves an altar for sacrifices, burnt offerings, or peace offerings apart from the altar of the Lord our God that stands before his tabernacle.

When Phinehas the priest, all the leaders of the people, and the commanders of thousands in Israel who were with him heard the words spoken by the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, they were pleased.

Phinehas, son of Eleazar, the priest of the Lord, said to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, ‘Today we know that the Lord is among us, because you have not committed this transgression before the Lord, and you have saved the Israelites from the Lord’s hand.’

Phinehas the priest, son of Eleazar, and the leaders of the clans returned from the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the Israelites, and delivered the report to them.

The report pleased the Israelites, and the Israelites blessed God. They spoke to the Israelites and said not to go up against them any longer in war to destroy the land of the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. And they settled in it.
Joshua named the altar of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and said, ‘For it is a witness among them that the Lord is their God.’
After many days, after the Lord had given Israel rest from all their enemies around them, Joshua was old and advanced in years.
Joshua called together all the Israelites, their elders, their leaders, their judges, and their scribes, and said to them, ‘I am old and advanced in years.’
You yourselves have seen everything the Lord our God did to all the nations he removed from before you, for the Lord God himself fought alongside you.
Now see that I have left you those remaining nations as an inheritance according to your tribes, from the Jordan—all the nations I destroyed—from the Great Sea, which forms the boundary in the west.

Now the Lord our God himself will destroy them before you until they perish. He will send wild beasts against them until he destroys them and their kings before you, and you will inherit their land, as the Lord our God promised us.
Now be very strong in taking care to do everything written in the book of the law of Moses, so that you do not turn aside from it to the right or to the left.
Lest you go among those nations that remain, do not let the names of their gods be mentioned among you. Do not swear by them, serve them, or bow down to them.
Instead, follow the Lord our God, as you have done to this day.
The Lord destroyed great and powerful nations before you, and no one has stood against you to this day.
One man among you put thousands to flight, because the Lord your God himself fought for you, as he promised you.
Take great care to love the Lord your God.
But if you turn back and join the nations that remain among you, and intermarry with them, and mingle with them and they with you,

Know for certain that the Lord will no longer destroy those nations before you. They will become snares and stumbling blocks for you, an obstacle at your heels and arrows in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the Lord your God gave you.

And now I am going today the way of everyone on earth. You know with all your heart and all your soul that not one word of all that the Lord your God spoke has failed. Everything has come to pass for you, and not one word of it has failed.

And just as all the good things that the Lord spoke concerning you have come upon you, so the Lord will bring upon you all the evil things, until he destroys you from this good land that the Lord your God gave you.

When you break the covenant of the Lord your God, which he commanded you to keep, and go to serve other gods and bow down to them, the Lord will be angry with you, and you will quickly perish from this good land that the Lord gave you.
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shiloh and summoned all the elders of Israel, their leaders, their scribes, and their judges, and they stood before the Lord.

Joshua spoke to all the people and said, “Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived as strangers beyond the River—Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor—and they served other gods.
And I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him throughout the land of the Canaanites, and multiplied his offspring and gave him Isaac.
I gave Isaac Jacob and Esau, and I gave Esau Mount Seir as an inheritance. But Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
There they became a great, numerous, and powerful nation. The Egyptians oppressed them, and the Lord struck the Egyptians with signs and wonders that he performed among them.
Then he brought you out of Egypt, and you entered the sea. The Egyptians pursued your ancestors with chariots and horses into the Red Sea.

You cried out to the Lord, and he placed a cloud and darkness between you and the Egyptians. He brought the sea upon them and covered them. Your own eyes saw what the Lord did to the land of the Egyptians, and you stayed in the wilderness for many days.

He brought you into the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. They fought against you, and the Lord delivered them into your hands. You took possession of their land and destroyed them before you.
Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up and fought against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
But the Lord your God did not wish to destroy you. Instead, he blessed you abundantly, rescued you from their hands, and delivered them into your hands.

You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The inhabitants of Jericho fought against you—the Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, Hittites, and Girgashites—and he delivered them into your hands.
He sent hornets ahead of you and drove them out before you—the twelve kings of the Amorites—not by your sword or your bow.
And the Lord gave you the land in which you had not labored, and you live in cities that you did not build, and you eat from vineyards and fig trees that you did not plant.
And now fear the Lord and serve him with integrity and righteousness. Put away the foreign gods that your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.

But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose today whom you will serve: the gods of your fathers who were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But I and my household will serve the Lord, for he is holy.
The people answered and said, “Far be it from us to forsake the Lord our God and serve foreign gods!”

For the Lord our God himself brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and performed those great signs for us, and protected us along the entire way we traveled and among all the nations through which we passed.
“And the Lord drove out the Amorites and all the nations living in the land from before us. We too will serve the Lord, for he is our God.”
And Joshua said to the people, “You cannot serve the Lord, for he is holy and jealous. He will not forgive your sins and lawless deeds.
“When you forsake the Lord and serve foreign gods, he will come upon you, afflict you, and destroy you in place of the good things he has done for you.”
And the people said to Joshua, “No, not so! We will serve the Lord.”
And Joshua said to the people, “See, you yourselves are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the Lord, to serve him.” And they said, “We are witnesses.”
And he said, “Now put away the foreign gods from among you, and direct your hearts toward the Lord, the God of Israel.”
And the people said to Joshua, “We will serve the Lord our God and obey his voice.”
And Joshua made a covenant with the people that day and gave them laws and judgments at Shiloh, before the tabernacle of the God of Israel.
And Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God. He took a large stone and set it up beneath the terebinth, before the Lord.

And Joshua said to all the people, “See, this stone will be a witness for you, for it has heard all the words spoken by the Lord, which he spoke to you today. It will be a witness for you in days to come, when you deal falsely with the Lord your God.”
And Joshua dismissed the people, and each went to his own place.
And Israel served the Lord throughout the days of Joshua and throughout the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had also seen all the works that the Lord had done in Israel.
And after this, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at the age of one hundred and ten.

And they buried him within the boundaries of his inheritance at Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash. There, where they buried him, they placed with him, as a memorial, the flint knives with which he had circumcised the sons of Israel at Gilgal when he brought them out of the land of the Egyptians, as the Lord had commanded. And they are there to this day.

And the sons of Israel brought Joseph’s bones up from Egypt and buried him at Shechem, in the portion of the field that Jacob had acquired from the Amorites living in Shechem for a hundred ewe lambs. He had given it to Joseph as his portion.

And after this, Eleazar the priest, the son of Aaron, died and was buried at Gibeah, belonging to his son Phinehas, which he had given him in the hill country of Ephraim. In those days the sons of Israel took the ark of the covenant of God and carried it around with them. And Phinehas served as priest in place of Eleazar his father until he died and was buried in his own Gibeah. And the sons of Israel went to their own places and their own cities. And the sons of Israel served Astarte and Ashtaroth and the gods of the nations around them. And the Lord delivered them into the hands of Eglon king of Moab, and he ruled over them for eighteen years.
